arxiv-2109-05983.title: Coupling between turbulence and solar-like oscillations: A combined Lagrangian PDF/SPH approach
arxiv-2109-05983.creator: J. Philidet, K. Belkacem, M.-J. Goupil
arxiv-2109-05983.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by J. Philidet, K. Belkacem, M.-J. Goupil. The development of space-borne missions such as CoRoT and Kepler now provides us with numerous and precise asteroseismic measurements that allow us to put better constraints on our theoretical knowledge of the physics of stellar interiors. In order to utilise the full potential of these measurements, however, we need a better theoretical understanding of the coupling between stellar oscillations and turbulent convection.

arxiv-2110-00955.title: Charm and multi-charm baryon measurements via strangeness tracking with the upgraded ALICE detector
arxiv-2110-00955.creator: \firstname David \lastname Dobrigkeit Chinellato for the ALICE Collaboration \fnsep
arxiv-2110-00955.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by \firstname David \lastname Dobrigkeit Chinellato for the ALICE Collaboration \fnsep. We present a new method for detection of multiply charmed baryons via their decays into strange baryons, using ‘strangeness tracking’. This method makes use of the state-of-the-art upgraded silicon detectors in ALICE during Runs 3, 4 and beyond will enable the novel possibility of tracking strange hadrons directly before they decay, leading to a very significant improvement in impact-parameter resolution.

arxiv-2202-03862.title: Casimir cosmology
arxiv-2202-03862.creator: Ulf Leonhardt
arxiv-2202-03862.description: Abstract In 1998 astronomers discovered that the expansion of the universe is accelerating. Somehow, something must have made gravity repulsive on cosmological scales. This something was called dark energy; it is described by Einstein’s cosmological constant; and it amounts to about 70% of the total mass of the universe.

arxiv-2211-08412.title: Evaluating the Factual Consistency of Large Language Models Through News Summarization
arxiv-2211-08412.creator: Derek Tam, Anisha Mascarenhas, Shiyue Zhang, Sarah Kwan, Mohit Bansal, Colin Raffel
arxiv-2211-08412.description: Abstract While large language models (LLMs) have proven to be effective on a large variety of tasks, they are also known to hallucinate information. To measure whether an LLM prefers factually consistent continuations of its input, we propose a new benchmark called FIB ( F actual I nconsistency B enchmark) that focuses on the task of summarization.

arxiv-2305-04483.title: Two dimensional solitary water waves with constant vorticity, Part I: the deep gravity case
arxiv-2305-04483.creator: James Rowan, Lizhe Wan
arxiv-2305-04483.description: Abstract . We consider the two dimensional pure gravity water waves with nonzero constant vorticity in infinite depth, working in the holomorphic coordinates introduced in [ 32 ] . We show that close to the critical velocity corresponding to zero frequency, a solitary wave exists.

arxiv-2305-05615.title: A discrete formulation of the Kane-Mele ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} invariant
arxiv-2305-05615.creator: Ken Shiozaki
arxiv-2305-05615.description: Abstract We present a discrete formulation of the Kane-Mele ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} invariant that is manifestly gauge-independent and quantized. In this short note, we present a formulation of the Kane-Mele \mathbb{Z}_{2} invariant Kane and Mele 2005 that does not require any gauge fixing conditions and is quantized for any discrete approximation of the Brillouin zone (BZ) torus.

arxiv-2408-02850.creator: Wesley G. Lautenschlaeger ∗ and Thaísa Tamusiunas
arxiv-2408-02850.description: Abstract . We develop a Galois theory of commutative rings under actions of finite inverse semigroups. We prove equivalences for the definition of Galois extension as well as a Galois correspondence theorem. We also discuss how the theory behaves in the case of inverse semigroups with zero. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary. 16W22. Secondary. 20M18, 13B05, 06A15. 1. Introduction S.

arxiv-2508-13787.title: BetaWeb: Towards a Blockchain-enabled Trustworthy Agentic Web
arxiv-2508-13787.creator: Zihan Guo, Yuanjian Zhou, Chenyi Wang, Linlin You, Minjie Bian, Weinan Zhang
arxiv-2508-13787.description: Abstract The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) has significantly propelled the development of artificial intelligence (AI) agents, which are increasingly evolving into diverse autonomous entities, advancing the LLM-based multi-agent systems (LaMAS). However, current agentic ecosystems remain fragmented and closed. Establishing an interconnected and scalable paradigm for Agentic AI has become a critical prerequisite.

Both the mutation rates and the lineages of influenza A viruses are likely

plos-pone-0008838.description: PLOS ONE research article. Rhodopsin, encoded by the gene Rhodopsin ( RH1 ), is extremely sensitive to light, and is responsible for dim-light vision. Bats are nocturnal mammals that inhabit poor light environments. Megabats (Old-World fruit bats) generally have well-developed eyes, while microbats (insect

pmc-11473972.title: Thyroid Artery Embolization for Tracheostomy Site Bleeding: A Report of Three Cases
pmc-11473972.creator: Suyoung Park, Jeong Ho Kim, Jung Han Hwang, Woo Sung Choi
pmc-11473972.description: In this case report, the authors present three cases of post-tracheostomy site bleeding successfully treated using embolization, supplemented by CT and angiography images. This report highlights that embolization can be a viable alternative when surgical or endoscopic interventions fail or are not applicable in cases of post-tracheostomy bleeding.

pmc-11519827.title: Antecedent Effect Models as an Exploratory Tool to Link Climate Drivers to Herbaceous Perennial Population Dynamics Data
pmc-11519827.creator: Aldo Compagnoni, Dylan Childs, Tiffany M Knight, Roberto Salguero‐Gómez
pmc-11519827.description: Understanding mechanisms and predicting natural population responses to climate is a key goal of Ecology. However, studies explicitly linking climate to population dynamics remain limited. Antecedent effect models are a set of statistical tools that capitalize on the evidence provided by climate and population data to select time windows correlated with a response (e.g., survival, reproduction).

pmc-11547392.title: Innovative Hybrid Nanocomposites in 3D Printing for Functional Applications: A Review
pmc-11547392.creator: Nguyen Thi Kim Tuyen, Dong Min Kim, Jung-Woo Lee, Jaehan Jung
pmc-11547392.description: 3D printing has garnered significant attention across academia and industry due to its capability to design and fabricate complex architectures. Applications such as those requiring intricate geometries or custom designs, including footwear, healthcare, energy storage, and electronics applications, greatly benefit from exploiting 3D printing processes.

pmc-11674391.title: Risk Factors for Low Back Pain in Youth Inline Hockey Players During the Season—A Prospective Cohort Research
pmc-11674391.creator: Antonio Cejudo, Víctor Jesús Moreno-Alcaraz, Pilar Sainz de Baranda, Andrea Martinuzzi, Hadas Nahman-Averbuch
pmc-11674391.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Low back pain is one of the most common musculoskeletal complaints in team sports. A screening test can help understand why injuries occur and predict who is at risk for non-contact low back pain.

pmc-11717401.title: The Assessment of TikTok as a Source of Quality Health Information on Human Papillomavirus: A Content Analysis
pmc-11717401.creator: Rhoda E Etta, Abdulhammed O Babatunde, Praise O Okunlola, Oluwatomisin K Akanbi, Kehinde J Adegoroye, Rofiat A Adepoju, Samuel T Tundealao
pmc-11717401.description: BackgroundVarious studies have evaluated the quality of health-related information on TikTok (ByteDance Ltd., Beijing, China), including topics such as COVID-19, diabetes, varicoceles, bladder cancer, colorectal cancer, and others. However, there is a paucity of data on studies that examined TikTok as a source of quality health information on human papillomavirus (HPV).

pmc-11862314.title: The approach of physiotherapists in the management of patients with persistent pain and comorbid anxiety/depression: are there any differences between male and female professionals?
pmc-11862314.creator: G Nicolini, M Chiesa, M Buoli
pmc-11862314.description: IntroductionChronic pain is a prevalent condition that is frequently complicated by concomitant mood and anxiety disorders. Very preliminary data indicate that female physiotherapists could have a better attitude towards psychiatric disorders.ObjectivesPurpose of the present article is to identify eventual differences in the management of patients with chronic pain and anxiety/mood disorders depending on the physiotherapists’ gender.

pmc-12565049.title: Autologous Tooth-Derived Biomaterials in Alveolar Bone Regeneration: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes and Histological Evidence
pmc-12565049.creator: Angelo Michele Inchingolo, Grazia Marinelli, Francesco Inchingolo, Roberto Vito Giorgio, Valeria Colonna, Benito Francesco Pio Pennacchio, Massimo Del Fabbro, Gianluca Tartaglia, Andrea Palermo, Alessio Danilo Inchingolo, Gianna Dipalma
pmc-12565049.description: Background: Autologous tooth-derived grafts have recently gained attention as an innovative alternative to conventional biomaterials for alveolar ridge preservation (ARP) and augmentation (ARA). Their structural similarity to bone and osteoinductive potential support clinical use. Methods: This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251108128).

pmc-12847734.title: PR inhibition stimulates G6PD expression to enhance malignancy in luminal breast cancer
pmc-12847734.creator: Jae Woong Jeong, Janghee Lee, Soong June Bae, Yoon Jin Cha, Sungsoon Fang, Hae-kyung Lee, Sung Gwe Ahn
pmc-12847734.description: Luminal breast cancer is the most prevalent and prognostic subtype of breast cancer. However, it has been reported that luminal breast cancer patients with lower progesterone receptor (PR) expression are associated with poor survival outcomes. Nevertheless, there is insufficient evidence linking PR expression to an aggressiveness of luminal breast cancer.

pmc-12989689.title: Exploring Chinese Herbal Medicines for Acute Kidney Injury: Pharmacological Mechanisms and Clinical Potential
pmc-12989689.creator: Yuan Zhou, Sijia Li, Minghai Shao, Yiling Qian, Tianying Lan, Dongsheng Yao, Tiantian Zhan, Tingting Li, Ziteng Shao, Chaoyang Ye, Shougang Zhuang
pmc-12989689.description: BackgroundAcute kidney injury (AKI) is a serious clinical condition marked by a rapid decline in renal function, leading to high morbidity, mortality, and healthcare burden. Despite advances in supportive care, effective pharmacologic therapies remain lacking, prompting interest in alternative approaches, including Chinese herbal medicines (CHMs).

pmc-13166881.title: Assessing the performance of a new diagnostic criterion for diagnosing esophageal lichen planus
pmc-13166881.creator: Anwesh Dash, Alexandra Strauss Starling, Sydney Shaffer, Amanda Muir, Kristle L Lynch
pmc-13166881.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Esophageal lichen planus (ELP) is a unique manifestation of lichen planus that is rarely studied. This disorder presents diagnostic challenges due to variable clinical presentations and the absence of universally accepted diagnostic criteria. This study evaluates the performance of the Schauer Diagnostic Criteria (SDC) in diagnosing ELP for two specific cohorts: patients with extra-esophageal manifestations of lichen planus (LP) and patients without extra-esophageal manifestations of LP. We analyzed esophageal biopsies with lichenoid patterns from a tertiary care center.

pmc-13284978.title: Development and validation of a machine learning–based model for diagnosing perioperative malnutrition in older adults with hip fracture
pmc-13284978.creator: Zhiqiang He, Mengyu Han, Yu An, Hui Xiao, Yaru Yang, Junxia Ye, Tianyu Wang, Jin Li
pmc-13284978.description: BackgroundThe prevalence of malnutrition is significant among older adults with hip fractures, while existing screening tools face challenges such as complex procedures and a limited ability to objectively classify malnutrition status. This study aimed to develop and test a machine learning–based diagnostic model for identifying malnutrition guided by the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria.

pmc-13665405.title: Exploring the Role of Umbilical Cord Blood Leptin and Visfatin in Fetal Growth: Associations with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Neonatal Anthropometric Measurements
pmc-13665405.creator: Maria Styliou, Angeliki Tiptiri-Kourpeti, Panagiotis Konstantaras, Panagiotis Tsikouras, Theopi Nalbanti, Nektaria Kritsotaki, Aggeliki Gerente, Konstantinos Nikolettos, Nikolaos Nikolettos
pmc-13665405.description: Leptin and visfatin are adipokines involved in metabolic regulation and fetal development, but their associations with maternal gestational diabetes mellitus and neonatal growth remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the relationships between umbilical cord blood leptin and visfatin concentrations, maternal GDM status, and neonatal anthropometric characteristics.
